Fill gaps in INMET climate time series using XGBoost

Source: R/sus_climate_fill_gap.R
sus_climate_fill_inmet.Rd

sus_climate_fill_inmet() imputes missing values in INMET automatic station data using station-wise XGBoost models with automated feature engineering.

Use it right after sus_climate_inmet() and before sus_climate_aggregate(), sus_climate_compute_indicators() or the heat/cold-wave functions. It is designed exclusively for hourly INMET data in the standard variable set (see below); it does not support UNIPLU data.

Key features:

  • Multi-target support: Impute one, many, or ALL known INMET variables in a single call

  • Station-wise modeling: Separate model per station per variable

  • Temporal features: Automatic creation of lags and rolling statistics

  • Quality control: Stations with >quality_threshold missing (per variable) are excluded

  • Parallel processing: Stations processed in parallel; workers resolved once and reused across all variable iterations

  • Evaluation mode: Assess accuracy by creating artificial gaps

Usage

sus_climate_fill_inmet(
  df,
  target_var,
  datetime_col = NULL,
  station_col = NULL,
  quality_threshold = 0.4,
  run_evaluation = FALSE,
  gap_percentage = 0.2,
  keep_features = FALSE,
  parallel = FALSE,
  workers = NULL,
  verbose = TRUE,
  lang = "pt"
)

Arguments

df

A data frame or climasus_df of hourly climate data, typically from sus_climate_inmet(). Must contain:

  • A datetime column (POSIXct or convertible; normally date)

  • A station identifier column (normally station_code)

  • The target numeric column(s) to be imputed

target_var

Character vector of column name(s) to impute, or the single string "all" to impute every one of the 17 known INMET variables present in df (errors if none is present). Names not found in df raise an error; names outside the known set are imputed with a warning. Examples:

  • Single variable: target_var = "tair_dry_bulb_c"

  • Multiple variables: target_var = c("tair_dry_bulb_c", "rh_mean_porc", "ws_2_m_s")

  • All known INMET variables: target_var = "all"

datetime_col

Single character string, name of the datetime column. If NULL (default), auto-detected.

station_col

Single character string, name of the station identifier column. If NULL (default), auto-detected.

quality_threshold

Numeric scalar in [0, 1]. Maximum allowed proportion of missing values of the target variable per station; stations above it are skipped for that variable. Default 0.4 (40%).

Recommended values for INMET data:

  • 0.3 (30%) - Conservative, high-quality stations only

  • 0.4 (40%) - Default, balanced approach

  • 0.6 (60%) - Lenient, includes stations with significant gaps

run_evaluation

Logical scalar. If TRUE, runs in evaluation mode instead of imputing:

  • Creates artificial MCAR gaps in observed data

  • Imputes and compares predictions with true values

  • Returns metrics by station

Default FALSE (production mode).

gap_percentage

Numeric scalar in (0, 1). Proportion of observed values set to missing in evaluation mode (MCAR: Missing Completely At Random). Ignored when run_evaluation = FALSE. Default 0.2 (20%).

keep_features

Logical scalar. If TRUE, retains engineered features (lags, rolling stats, time features). Default FALSE (returns only original columns plus the is_imputed_<var> flags).

parallel

Logical scalar. If TRUE, processes stations in parallel using furrr/future (multisession); falls back to sequential with a warning if these packages are missing. Default FALSE.

workers

Single positive integer, or NULL (default). Number of parallel workers; NULL uses max(1, availableCores() - 1). Ignored if parallel = FALSE. The value is resolved once at the start and reused across all variable iterations, avoiding repeated plan switches.

verbose

Logical scalar. If TRUE (default), prints progress messages.

lang

Single character string. Message language: "pt" (Portuguese), "en" (English), or "es" (Spanish). Default "pt".

Value

Production mode (run_evaluation = FALSE): a climasus_df (stage "climate", type "filled", system = NULL) with the same columns as df, imputed values in each target_var and one logical flag column is_imputed_<var> per variable. sus_meta() records the source, imputed variables, per-variable imputation stats and quality_threshold. Stations that fail the quality threshold are removed from the output (see Methodological Notes).

Evaluation mode (run_evaluation = TRUE): a plain named list (one element per variable that had at least one eligible station), each with:

  • $data: tibble with date, the station column, true_value and pred_value for the artificial gaps

  • $metrics: tibble with per-station performance metrics:

    • station_id: Station identifier

    • rmse: Root Mean Squared Error

    • mae: Mean Absolute Error

    • r_squared: R-squared (closer to 1 is better)

    • smape: Symmetric MAPE (0-200%, lower is better)

    • slope_bias: Slope of predicted vs. true; close to 1.0 means no systematic under/over-estimation

    • gap_percentage, gap_mechanism: evaluation settings

The result of evaluation mode can be passed to sus_climate_plot_fill().

INMET Variable Set

The function is optimized for the following 17 INMET variables:

  • Atmospheric Pressure: patm_mb, patm_max_mb, patm_min_mb

  • Temperature: tair_dry_bulb_c, tair_max_c, tair_min_c

  • Dew Point: dew_tmean_c, dew_tmax_c, dew_tmin_c

  • Relative Humidity: rh_max_porc, rh_min_porc, rh_mean_porc

  • Precipitation: rainfall_mm

  • Wind: ws_gust_m_s, ws_2_m_s, wd_degrees

  • Solar Radiation: sr_kj_m2

When target_var = "all", the function automatically detects and imputes only these 17 variables if present in the data. Other numeric columns can be imputed by naming them explicitly (a warning is shown). Variable-specific transforms are applied internally (log1p for rainfall, sqrt for wind and solar radiation); humidity and wind direction are rounded to integers after imputation.

Methodological Notes

Important limitations:

  • Not forecasting: Predicts only where data are missing

  • Station independence: Models don't share information between stations

  • Quality filter: Stations with >quality_threshold missing are skipped and dropped from the returned data

  • Minimum data: A station needs at least 30 observed values per variable

  • Features may use neighbouring (past and future) hours, so this is interpolation, not prediction

Feature engineering: Automatically creates:

  • Time features: hour, day, month, year, cyclic transforms

  • Lag features (past, forward and seasonal) at 1, 2, 3, 12, 24, 168 periods

  • Rolling statistics (mean, sd, ...) over windows 3, 6, 12, 24

A fixed seed (42) is set for reproducibility.

Evaluation Mode Details

When run_evaluation = TRUE, the function:

  1. Creates artificial gaps (MCAR)

  2. Runs imputation on the data with gaps

  3. Compares predictions with true values

  4. Returns per-station performance

This helps assess model accuracy before production use.

See also

  • sus_climate_inmet() to import the input data

  • sus_climate_plot_fill() to visualise results and metrics

  • sus_climate_aggregate() to join the filled series with health data

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
climate_data <- sus_climate_inmet(years = 2023, uf = "SP")

# ===== PRODUCTION MODE - single variable =====
filled_temp <- sus_climate_fill_inmet(
  df = climate_data,
  target_var = "tair_dry_bulb_c",
  quality_threshold = 0.3,
  parallel = TRUE
)

# ===== PRODUCTION MODE - multiple variables =====
filled_multi <- sus_climate_fill_inmet(
  df = climate_data,
  target_var = c("tair_dry_bulb_c", "rh_mean_porc", "ws_2_m_s"),
  quality_threshold = 0.3,
  parallel = TRUE,
  workers = 4
)

# ===== PRODUCTION MODE - all known INMET variables =====
filled_all <- sus_climate_fill_inmet(
  df = climate_data,
  target_var = "all",
  parallel = TRUE
)

# ===== EVALUATION MODE - single variable =====
eval_results <- sus_climate_fill_inmet(
  df = climate_data,
  target_var = "ws_2_m_s",
  run_evaluation = TRUE,
  gap_percentage = 0.2,
  parallel = TRUE,
  workers = 4
)
eval_results$ws_2_m_s$metrics

# ===== EVALUATION MODE - multiple variables =====
eval_multi <- sus_climate_fill_inmet(
  df = climate_data,
  target_var = c("tair_dry_bulb_c", "ws_2_m_s"),
  run_evaluation = TRUE,
  gap_percentage = 0.2
)
eval_multi$tair_dry_bulb_c$metrics
eval_multi$ws_2_m_s$metrics
} # }
